issues: All three quotes re-fetched 2026-09-23 and --check FOUND. The charter paragraph is verbatim (charter-ietf-aipref-01, Approved). The history page shows '2025-01-07 Cindy Morgan Charter approved, group active', and the charter document history shows 'IESG has approved the charter' on 2025-01-07, so 'chartered 7 January 2025' is right. draft-ietf-aipref-vocab-08 is dated 14 September 2026 in the draft header (Datatracker's 'Last updated' reads 2026-09-13, a UTC timing difference). It is an 'Active Internet-Draft (aipref WG)' with IESG state 'I-D Exists', so 'still an Internet-Draft' is right. The Aug 2026 milestone for sending it to the IESG has passed.

legalForce 'None' overstates the case. The charter does list 'Technical enforcement of preferences' as out of scope, and §3.2 of the draft says it does not 'ensure that preferences are followed'. But the draft's Introduction says: 'The vocabulary is intended to be used in jurisdictions where expressing preferences results in legal obligations, as well as where there are no associated legal obligations.' So the spec carries no legal force of its own, but an AIPREF signal can carry legal effect where local law gives a machine-readable reservation force. The field is corrected and a source added.

Minor: the vocab draft defines the author of a preference as any 'Declaring party', not necessarily an organisation, and warns that 'no assumptions can be made about where a preference originates'. whoProffers='organisation' is acceptable only with the note's 'usually'.

fieldFixes.legalForce: None of its own: the charter puts technical enforcement out of scope and the draft does not ensure preferences are followed; the draft says the vocabulary is meant for use both where expressing preferences results in legal obligations and where it does not

issues: Both quotes re-fetched fresh (not from cache) on 2026-09-23 and --check FOUND. The IEEE SA page shows Status Active Standard, PAR Approval 2017-12-06, Board Approval 2025-11-04, Published 2026-01-20, Standard Committee SSIT/SC, WG MRPT-WG, and chair Doc Searls. 'Approved 4 November 2025; published 20 January 2026' and the body field are correct.

Three claims were not in any quoted text: 'launched 28 January 2026', 'five agreements in a market-feedback phase', and 'roster kept by Customer Commons'. All three are correct according to other pages. Doc Searls' 'Now We Begin' (posted 2026-01-29; WP API date 2026-01-29T14:40) says 'Yesterday, Customer Commons and MyData Global launched MyTerms'. myterms.info/ieee7012-standards/ says it will launch with 5 agreements for up to 6 months of market feedback. The FAQ says the roster is posted at a neutral nonprofit site such as CustomerCommons.org or MyTerms.info, and the myterms.info footer reads '© 2026 Customer Commons'. Sources for these are added.

Caveat: the market-feedback phase was announced as 'up to 6 months' from the 28 Jan 2026 launch, so by today (2026-09-23) that window has passed. No source read says whether updated agreements or a 'full market launch' followed. The fate text describes the launch state, which is accurate.
The FAQ says the agreements are 'enforceable by contract law'. That is the proponents' claim, and the record correctly flags it as untested in court.
